## Problem Analysis
Kea’s existing selector memoization compares inputs rather than tracking nested reads, so unrelated state changes can trigger unnecessary computation. An opt-in atomic engine needs a reliable dependency graph, selective updates and subscriptions, and health reporting without disrupting existing behavior.

## Suggested Directions
- First assess branch availability and task constraints separately; an available revision may be useful only if it is an authorized equivalent.
- Trace selector registration and reducer access to understand stable identities, precise read tracking, and dependencies across selectors.
- Consider collection semantics, conditional reads, and complete cycle detection alongside ordinary nested state dependencies.
- Explore transaction-level propagation that avoids duplicate work and distinguishes invalidated inputs from changed outputs.
- Keep engine state and health reporting scoped to the appropriate context and logic, while preserving disabled-mode and lifecycle behavior.
- Examine React snapshot and subscription semantics, then use focused tests and the existing suite to check precision and compatibility.

## Key Location Clues
- `src/core/selectors.ts` — Registers derived selectors and is central to identity, dependency tracking, and evaluation counts.
- `src/core/reducers.ts` — Creates reducer selectors and locates logic state for tracking.
- `src/core/index.ts` — Provides the dispatch boundary relevant to state comparison and update scheduling.
- `src/kea/atomic.ts` — The reference design places the new atomic engine in a separate module absent from the baseline.
- `src/kea/context.ts` — Defines context options and lifecycle boundaries for engine isolation.
- `src/kea/kea.ts` — Exposes built-logic fields through wrappers, including possible health access.
- `src/react/hooks.ts` — Contains selector subscriptions and value hooks whose snapshot behavior needs attention.
- `src/types.ts` — Describes public logic, context options, and health API types.
- `src/kea/mount.ts` — Establishes lifecycle ordering that atomic integration should preserve.
- `test/jest/events.js`, `test/jest/plugins.js`, and `test/jest/hooks.js` — Provide existing lifecycle, plugin, and React integration coverage.

## Critical Warnings
- Avoid assuming an available revision safely substitutes for a missing named base: task constraints may forbid it; check for an authorized equivalent and, if none is established, report the specific blocker and seek clarification.
